title: Uffizi Galleries: Masterpieces
subtitle: Twenty paintings in which posture, clothing and proportion carry the argument.
introduction:
Botticelli's Venus is arriving, not being born: the winds bring her towards a waiting cloak. That distinction gives the picture a direction. Across this selection, bodies do similarly practical work. They establish authority, bring a sacred event close, arrest a battle or make a killing physically comprehensible. A bent elbow may explain more than a label naming a style.

The repeated Madonnas are useful comparisons rather than interruptions between famous pictures. A throne can hold a figure apart from the surrounding world; an angel's glance can bring that world closer. Follow these changes without treating every departure from ordinary anatomy as a mistake waiting to be corrected.
visitNote: This is a selection from the Uffizi collection, not a room-by-room itinerary through all the Uffizi Galleries sites. Loans and installations change. Check the museum’s visitor information and individual collection records before planning a visit around one work.

books.title: A Treatise on Painting
books.author: Leonardo da Vinci; translated by John Francis Rigaud
books.note: Leonardo’s collected writings discuss proportion, movement, light and the arrangement of figures. They offer practical questions to bring back to the paintings here, including his own Annunciation.

works.title: The Birth of Venus
works.credit: Sandro Botticelli. The Birth of Venus. Image: WikiArt. Public domain (WikiArt label). Proportionally resized and JPEG compressed; no crop.
works.description: The shell has reached the shore, but the movement continues through Venus's hair and the cloak held out to receive her. Botticelli gives the arriving figure little of the weight a body would need to stand securely there. The long contours keep her connected to wind and fabric, suspended between the journey and its end.

works.title: The Annunciation
works.credit: Annunciation. WikiArt; Leonardo da Vinci. Proportional resizing and JPEG compression; source frame preserved.
works.description: The lectern and garden wall give the encounter firm boundaries. Beyond them, Leonardo allows water and mountains to become progressively less distinct. Mary and the angel therefore meet in a space that feels close and measurable, while the world behind them escapes that clarity. Nearness and distance are painted differently, rather than merely made different sizes.

works.title: Medusa
works.credit: Caravaggio. Medusa. Image: WikiArt. Public domain (WikiArt label). Proportionally resized and JPEG compressed; no crop.
works.description: The open mouth registers a cry that the severed head can no longer sustain. Blood below and snakes above leave almost no neutral passage around the face. Caravaggio painted on a convex shield: the support projects towards the viewer even as the depicted head seems caught in an uncertain space within it. The object complicates the illusion.

works.title: Venus of Urbino
works.credit: Titian. Venus of Urbino. Image: WikiArt. Public domain (WikiArt label). Proportionally resized and JPEG compressed; no crop.
works.description: Titian gives this Venus something Botticelli's lacks: a household continuing behind her. The maids attend to a chest, and the dog sleeps while the reclining woman looks out. Those different states of attention make the gaze unusually direct. The Uffizi reads the domestic details in relation to marriage, placing the exposed body within a social setting.

works.title: Ognissanti Madonna
works.credit: Giotto di Bondone. Madonna in Maest (Ognissanti Madonna). Image: WikiArt. Public domain (WikiArt label). Proportionally resized and JPEG compressed; no crop.
works.description: Mary's greater scale establishes her sacred rank before any gesture does. Yet Giotto also makes the robe contain a seated body, supported by a throne with architectural depth. Neither effect cancels the other. The image can assert a hierarchy while allowing the central figure to occupy space with an intelligible physical weight.

works.title: Adoration of the Magi
works.credit: Gentile da Fabriano. Adoration of the Magi. Image credit: Gentile da Fabriano. Wikimedia Commons. Public domain (https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/mark/1.0/). Resized and JPEG-compressed; selected source frame preserved.
works.description: The procession is already under way in the distant hills before it arrives at the child. Gentile da Fabriano turns looking across the painting into a way of following that journey. The elaborate clothes and horses crowd its destination, but the landscape prevents the encounter from becoming an isolated ceremonial group: these visitors have come from somewhere.

works.title: Judith Beheading Holofernes
works.credit: Artemisia Gentileschi, Judith Beheading Holofernes. Uffizi Galleries, Florence. Reproduction via Wikimedia Commons (PD-Art). Source reproduction has a levels adjustment. Full-frame proportional resize and JPEG compression to at most 100,000 bytes; no crop or generated content.
works.description: Follow the arms before trying to separate the figures. Judith and her attendant have different jobs, and their crossed limbs show how tightly the action depends on both women. Artemisia makes resistance and effort visible through braced bodies. The violence is not explained by a symbol or an expression alone; it has a difficult physical procedure.

works.title: Rucellai Madonna
works.credit: Duccio. Madonna Rucellai. Image: WikiArt. Public domain (WikiArt label). Proportionally resized and JPEG compressed; no crop.
works.description: The gold edging of Mary's robe gives the eye a route through the large blue shape. Its turns suggest where the body changes direction without dissolving the ceremonial clarity of the figure. Duccio's angels support the throne rather than share an ordinary room with its occupant. Delicate handling and emphatic hierarchy belong to the same image.

works.title: Adoration of the Magi
works.catalogueTitle: Adoration of the Magi, central panel from the Altarpiece
works.credit: Adoration of the Magi, central panel from the Altarpiece. WikiArt; Andrea Mantegna. Proportional resizing and JPEG compression; source frame preserved.
works.description: Mantegna's rocky opening makes a narrow destination for the approaching visitors. The procession has to negotiate the terrain before reaching Mary and the child. Compare Gentile's crowded, richly furnished arrival: here the rock carries much of the organising work, enclosing the meeting while the thin route behind it preserves the distance travelled.

works.title: Primavera
works.credit: Sandro Botticelli. The Spring. Image: WikiArt. Public domain (WikiArt label). Proportionally resized and JPEG compressed; no crop.
works.description: Begin with the changing kinds of movement: pursuit at the right, a dance elsewhere, a more stationary centre. Botticelli keeps the groups distinct even as repeated contours connect them beneath the trees. The painting's larger meanings remain debated. Its gestures offer a firmer first foothold than a key that claims to translate every figure into one settled message.

works.title: Battista Sforza
works.credit: Portrait of Battista Sforza. WikiArt; Piero della Francesca. Proportional resizing and JPEG compression; source frame preserved.
works.description: The profile refuses the exchange of glances offered by Titian's Venus. Battista's face is sharply bounded, while the landscape behind it extends far beyond the sitter's immediate space. Piero makes stillness a form of public presentation. Jewels and the patterned bodice specify status, but the unyielding outline gives the portrait its compositional authority.

works.title: The Battle of San Romano: The Unhorsing of Bernardino della Ciarda
works.credit: Victory over Bernardino della Ciarda. WikiArt; Paolo Uccello. Proportional resizing and JPEG compression; source frame preserved.
works.description: Fallen weapons divide the ground beneath the colliding horses. Their clear directions let the eye measure a space whose occupants are engaged in violent disorder. Uccello keeps both systems visible: the battle as bodily confusion and the painting as an arrangement of lines. The ordered surface does not make the subject any less brutal.

works.title: Fortitude
works.credit: Sandro Botticelli. Fortitude. WikiArt source label: Public domain. Proportional resize and JPEG compression; no crop. Source: https://www.wikiart.org/en/sandro-botticelli/fortitude-1470-1
works.description: Botticelli gives a virtue a seat, armour and a contained gesture. Fortitude does not need to demonstrate her strength by striking an opponent. The supported body and firm grasp establish the quality through readiness rather than action. Broad red cloth supplies a different kind of surface against which the harder armour can register.

works.title: Madonna and Child with Two Angels
works.credit: Filippo Lippi. Madonna and Child. Image credit: Filippo Lippi. Wikimedia Commons. Public domain (https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/mark/1.0/). Resized and JPEG-compressed; selected source frame preserved.
works.description: One angel turns away from the devotional exchange and smiles out of the picture. That small departure changes the group's relationship with its audience. Mary keeps her hands joined, the child remains supported, and the sacred arrangement holds; Filippo Lippi nonetheless leaves a point at which an ordinary, sociable glance crosses its boundary.

works.title: Harbour with the Villa Medici
works.credit: Claude Lorrain. Harbour with Villa Medici. WikiArt source label: Public domain. Proportional resize and JPEG compression; no crop. Source: https://www.wikiart.org/en/claude-lorrain/harbour-with-villa-medici-1637
works.description: The buildings and ships supply substantial forms, but their placement opens a passage towards the harbour's light. Claude's small foreground workers establish a human scale without taking possession of the scene. This imagined port offers a useful reversal of the figure paintings: people occupy a world organised primarily around distance rather than around them.

works.title: Lucrezia Panciatichi
works.credit: Bronzino. Lucrezia Panciatichi. WikiArt source label: Public domain. Proportional resize and JPEG compression; no crop. Source: https://www.wikiart.org/en/agnolo-bronzino/lucrezia-panciatichi-1540
works.description: The book gives a resting place to the hand; jewellery and dark trim break the broad expanse of red satin. Bronzino distributes these details around a face that remains remarkably still. The portrait makes social presentation legible through controlled surfaces. It supplies evidence of dress and bearing, not unrestricted access to the sitter's private character.

works.title: Madonna and Child with Saints Dionysius, Dominic, Clement and Thomas Aquinas
works.catalogueTitle: Madonna and Child enthroned with St. Dionysius, Aeropagita, Domenic, Clement and Thomas Aquinas
works.credit: Madonna and Child enthroned with St. Dionysius, Aeropagita, Domenic, Clement and Thomas Aquinas. WikiArt; Domenico Ghirlandaio. Proportional resizing and JPEG compression; source frame preserved.
works.description: The architectural recess establishes a centre that the saints can share without standing in identical poses. Ghirlandaio varies their heights through kneeling and standing, while the floor and arches hold the assembly together. The setting performs an important task: separate figures become occupants of a coherent space rather than a row of isolated sacred portraits.

works.title: Madonna and Child with Six Saints
works.catalogueTitle: Madonna and Child with Six Saints
works.credit: Sandro Botticelli. Madonna and Child with Six Saints. WikiArt source label: Public domain. Proportional resize and JPEG compression; no crop. Source: https://www.wikiart.org/en/sandro-botticelli/madonna-and-child-with-six-saints
works.description: The kneeling saints occupy the nearest part of the patterned floor. They help negotiate the distance to the elevated Virgin and child, while turns of heads lead the eye between the figures. In this Botticelli, small changes of posture give a still group its structure. Compare the more conspicuous movements of *Primavera*: here a quiet pose can do the compositional work.

works.title: Madonna and Child with Saint John the Baptist and Saint Sebastian
works.catalogueTitle: Madonna and Child with St. John the Baptist and St. Sebastian
works.credit: Madonna and Child with St. John the Baptist and St. Sebastian. WikiArt; Pietro Perugino. Proportional resizing and JPEG compression; source frame preserved.
works.description: The saints stand apart, with open intervals around their bodies. Perugino makes those gaps as easy to read as the figures themselves. Repeated arches reinforce the separation without breaking the group into unrelated parts. Where other altarpieces gather attention through a crowd, this arrangement gives each presence room and keeps the approach to Mary clear.

works.title: Madonna of the Long Neck
works.credit: Parmigianino. Madonna with the Long Neck. WikiArt source label: Public domain. Proportional resize and JPEG compression; no crop. Source: https://www.wikiart.org/en/parmigianino/madonna-with-the-long-neck-1540
works.description: The crowded angels and the open space beside the column refuse an even distribution. Mary's extended neck, long fingers and unusually proportioned child continue the imbalance within the bodies themselves. Parmigianino gives no single comfortable scale against which to settle everything. After the measured intervals of Perugino, the picture makes the usefulness of stable proportion conspicuous by withdrawing it.

closingSections.title: Choose a comparison, not a checklist
paragraphs: Try following one problem through three works: how a hand holds, how clothing describes a body, or how a throne creates distance. The collection selection is not a room-by-room route. Check the Uffizi's current notices and individual display information before arranging a visit around a particular painting.
